content: Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning to have surgery, or if you will be confined to a bed or chair for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight). These conditions can increase your risk of developing blood clots. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of ospemifene from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. You should undergo a complete physical examination, including breast and pelvic exams, and a PAP test (to screen for vaginal cancer) as directed by your doctor, typically at least once a year. Periodic mammograms should also be performed as determined by your doctor. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts. Report any unusual vaginal bleeding, breast pain, or lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Ospemifene may increase your risk of uterine cancer. It may also rarely cause serious blood clots in the legs or lungs. Inform your doctor if you have a history of blood clots (e.g., deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism). Discuss with your doctor the risk factors for developing strokes (which can sometimes be fatal) while taking this medication. Risk factors include tobacco use, alcohol use, high cholesterol, diabetes, or a history of heart disease. This medication is used to treat painful sexual intercourse and vaginal dryness in women after menopause. It is different from hormones (such as estrogens and progestins) and works by acting like estrogen in certain parts of the body. Read the Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist before you start taking ospemifene and each time you get a refill. Use this medication regularly to gain the most benefit from it. Possible side effects include hot flashes, vaginal discharge, muscle spasms, and sweating. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious problems from blood clots (e.g., heart attack, stroke, blood clots in the lungs or legs). You may be at increased risk for blood clots if you are severely dehydrated, have a history of blood clots, heart or blood vessel disease, heart failure, stroke, or if you are immobile (e.g., during very long plane flights or being bedridden). If you have any of these conditions, report them to your doctor or pharmacist before using this medication. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
